quest.title: New Shoots from Old Branches
quest.description: As you and Paimon pass by Ogura Textiles & Kimonos, you bump into two rather familiar people...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x650, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? Those two look familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, it's Ippei and Shinnojou!

choices.text: So it is!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, guess they must be good friends, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, let's go say hi.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hi, Ippei! Hi, Shinnojou! What are you guys doing here?

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: Oh! It's you! Thanks so much for your help last time.

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: I was just ordering some clothes when I ran into him.

response.speaker: Shinnojou
response.text: You know these two as well?

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: Yes. They helped me and Master Kamaji out a great deal last time. I've never had the chance to say thank you properly.

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: What about you? How do you know them?

response.speaker: Shinnojou
response.text: Also a chance encounter. Our Lady had them join us as additional guards for a goods escort in order to sneak out of Ritou undetected.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So we all know each other, huh! What a coincidence!

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: Ah, not exactly. We've only just met. We both came here to order some clothes and got to chatting.

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: Somehow we ended up on the topic of Master Kamaji and Lady Hiiragi's relationship... Wait... it's okay to talk about that, right?

response.speaker: Shinnojou
response.text: It's probably fine. They've known about it for a long time already.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah! Paimon remembers those two had a thing. In fact, that was why Chisato wanted us to deliver a letter!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's old news though, so why's it come up now? Are they... taking the next step, or something?

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: We have reason to suspect that they'll be getting married soon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! That's great! They can finally make it official!

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: Of course, this is just personal speculation. They haven't announced anything, and we wouldn't dare to ask...

response.speaker: Shinnojou
response.text: I was instructed to place an order for some formal wear for a big banquet. Turns out that Ippei received the exact same instructions as I did.

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: They're both preparing for a banquet at the same time, they're both purchasing the kind of fine wine and confectionery normally reserved for big festivals... It's hard not to put two and two together.

response.speaker: Shinnojou
response.text: Lady Hiiragi has been in high spirits recently, and I heard she's on a diet as well... Surely it's all for the wedding.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is wonderful news! But, um...

response.speaker: Shinnojou
response.text: What's wrong?

response.speaker: Shinnojou
response.text: Oh, don't mind me. She's about to be happily married to the love of her life. I genuinely couldn't be happier for her.

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: Right? I think so, too, it's fantastic!

response.speaker: Shinnojou
response.text: Yes, but we shouldn't let ourselves get overexcited. What if it's all a big misunderstanding? As things stand, we have no actual proof of a wedding.

response.speaker: Shinnojou
response.text: Now, if they sent me out to deliver wedding invitations, that would be a different story...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Shinnojou doesn't look like he's taking this very well at all.

choices.text: You seem upset.

response.speaker: Shinnojou
response.text: ...Sorry. I just... haven't slept well recently.

response.speaker: Shinnojou
response.text: I'm ashamed to be so out of sorts at work. I'm not living up to my responsibilities, either to the Kanjou Commission or to my lady...

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: Are you worried about their wedding?

response.speaker: Shinnojou
response.text: Not exactly, it's just... everything feels kind of up in the air until they make it official.

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: I get what you mean, I really do! We need this wedding to be set in stone before the celebrations can really begin!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Actually, you don't get what he means at all...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What should we do? Shall we just... straight up ask them?

response.speaker: Ippei
response.text: I don't know, that seems a bit rude...

choices.text: Well, since this is a wedding between two Commissions...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! If Ayaka knows about it, that means it's a sure thing!

response.speaker: Shinnojou
response.text: I... I don't think it's a good idea to bother the Yashiro Commission about this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Ah, it's fine. {NICKNAME} and Ayaka are practically best buds. There's nothing to worry about!

response.speaker: Shinnojou
response.text: I see... Then, thank you, thank you very much. Having a definite answer will stop my thoughts from running wild.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go to the Kamisato Estate!

choices.text: The Yashiro Commission oversees wedding ceremonies. They'll know something.
You seem down.
Remind me who they are again?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? You forgot already?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That one is Shinnojou. Back when we first arrived in Inazuma, we escorted Hiiragi Chisato out of Ritou with him. Remember? That's how we got out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Next to him is Ippei, Kujou Kamaji's servant. That day when we hung out with Ei, he came and told us that Kujou Kamaji had gone missing. He was really worried.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Good memory.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, all part of Paimon's job as your guide.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, let's go say hi.

talks.objective: Meet Ayaka at the Kamisato Estate

dialogues.speaker: Ippei
dialogues.text: This place impresses me every time I come here. It's so magnificent but still so elegant.

dialogues.speaker: Shinnojou
dialogues.text: We'll just wait here. We don't want to cause any extra trouble for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ayaka wouldn't mind!

dialogues.speaker: Ippei
dialogues.text: Honestly, even if we did come with you, we wouldn't know what to say or do once we were inside... Hehe, so we'll just leave you to it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright then. We won't be long.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Greetings, both. I have long been indebted to you on my sister's behalf. Finally, I have the chance to express my profoundest gratitude to you in person.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Ayaka is out today. If you are here regarding anything related to the Kamisato Clan, you are quite welcome to discuss it with me instead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... hi... Your flattering words... flatter us. Um, please excuse the sudden... -ness of our visit, for it is most improper etiquette...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Hahaha, why on earth are you talking like that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, he seems like a pretty powerful person... He's already working his way up Paimon's list of people to never mess with...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look! As soon as he stands up, the whole atmosphere in the room changes and it feels like you've gotta be super polite!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Haha, you shower me with praise undeserved, my little guest.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: There is no need to be quite so formal. This is a private residence, so please relax.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, good! 'Cause that whole spiel was really tiring just now! Alright, now that that's over, Paimon's just gonna ask the question.

choices.text: Paimon goes from polite to presumptuous in a split-second.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We heard a rumor that Kujou Kamaji and Hiiragi Chisato are gonna get married soon. Do you know anything about that?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Oh? I wouldn't have thought you'd heard about that yet.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: As it happens, we've crossed paths with them before.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I see... Well, it's true. It wasn't long ago that I received the news myself.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: The head clans of two Commissions are to become joined through marriage. This is big news, for the whole of Inazuma.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Since the Yashiro Commission presides over cultural and ceremonial affairs, it closely involves us, too.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Yes. And since the commissions are kind of the face of the Almighty Shogun to the masses, this wedding is one that we have to treat as a serious affair.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, makes sense.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, two true lovers becoming husband and wife. What a happy occasion!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: It is. High-profile matrimonial links between two commissions are extremely rare, but these two truly love each other. Tradition should give way to freedom in this case.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Alright then. I'll be sure to pay them a visit to send the best wishes of the Kamisato Clan.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: No need. I'll visit them personally this time.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Huh? But you have other things to be doing...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: This is a marriage between the Kujou Clan and the Hiiragi Clan. The Kamisato Clan must demonstrate an appropriate level of respect.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: The work of the Yashiro Commission is indeed multifarious. Normally, weddings and other ceremonies would come under the supervision of my sister.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: But she is presently occupied with other matters, and I happen to have a little time to spare. This will be a good chance for me to pay a visit to the bride and groom.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Oh — and would you two care to join me?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You mean us?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I presume you two have a special connection with the individuals in question, or you would not be quite so interested in this matter.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: This being the case, why not come and offer your best wishes too? Or... is my presumption incorrect?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, it's not as interesting as you make it sound... No special connections here. Super-ordinary ones, actually.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We just agreed to help deliver a letter this one time, that's all... Although, wait... does that mean we helped make this wedding happen!?

choices.text: Paimon, don't overestimate your contribution here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, alright then...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But still. Let's go see them.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I cannot thank you enough. Your mere presence shall surely mean we are spared the futile pursuit known as small talk.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you're the Yashiro Commissioner, but you can't do small talk?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Ahaha... small talk is a chore. Of course, there are some people in the world who quite enjoy doing chores... but I am not one of them.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Thoma, I'm heading out with my two guests now. I'll leave the residence in your capable hands.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Not a problem. Take care, my lord.

choices.text: Romantic relationships are determined by fate.
So adaptable, Paimon.

talks.objective: Talk to Thoma and Kamisato Ayato
Report back to Ippei and Shinnojou

dialogues.speaker: Ippei
dialogues.text: Ahh, you're finally—

dialogues.speaker: Shinnojou
dialogues.text: Ah! Yashiro Commissioner!?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Hmm? Who are these two?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They're friends of ours. Paimon will do the introductions!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You introduce your companions to Ayato and update Ippei and Shinnojou on the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Shinnojou
dialogues.text: So it's true...

dialogues.speaker: Shinnojou
dialogues.text: Well, there we have it... That's it, then. So be it.

dialogues.speaker: Ippei
dialogues.text: Great! So our hunch was spot on!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: It is a little inappropriate for me to have shared news of this magnitude with you. So I would be much obliged if you could keep it in strict confidence until an official public announcement is made.

dialogues.speaker: Ippei
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Sir. We... we give you our word, we won't tell anyone about it!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: That puts my mind at ease. Now, on the topic, we'd like to pay a visit to the Kujou Clan. Would you mind leading the way for us?

dialogues.speaker: Ippei
dialogues.text: Of course not. I'd be honored!

dialogues.speaker: Shinnojou
dialogues.text: I guess this is where I... Goodbye, then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cheer up, Shinnojou!

dialogues.speaker: Shinnojou
dialogues.text: I'll try. Thank you.

talks.objective: Go to the Kujou Estate and talk to Kujou Kamaji

dialogues.speaker: Ippei
dialogues.text: Alright then. Please excuse me, I'll leave you to it from here.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: Okay. Thanks, Ippei.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I apologize that your impromptu visit comes at a busy time for us, Commissioner. Otherwise, you can be sure that we would've prepared a more extravagant reception.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I don't mean to impose, Sir Kujou. In fact, I'm not here on official business at all.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I heard the good news about yourself and Lady Hiiragi. What a glorious marital alliance this shall be. Given the close ties between our clans, it seemed only right that I should come and offer the Kamisato Clan's congratulations in person.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I'm truly honored. I hope the news didn't come as too much of a surprise...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there! We came to congratulate you as well!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How have you been?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: Since the incident with the Takatsukasa Clan, things in the Tenryou Commission have slowly started to stabilize.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I'm still acclimating to the position of acting head of the Clan. I just hope I'm up to the task, so I can live up to everyone's expectations.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: You're far too modest. The public thinks very highly of you. They say you're hard-working, upright, and responsible.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I'm flattered, but I wouldn't have achieved anything without the support of my people. Thanks to them, everything is gradually stabilizing, and I've finally had the chance to focus a little on my personal life.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, well you're certainly making big progress in that department!

choices.text: Sounds like it was worth sending that letter.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Hehe, come on now. You're embarrassing me...

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Ah! Pardon me, I, um...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: It's perfectly alright. Please, continue. I'm quite content to listen.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: It's a joyous occasion. Light-hearted is exactly how things should be. Really, who stays stony-faced when talking about a wedding?

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: You're right.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: But I am curious to know — what's your honest opinion on the whole thing? Do you think it's... too sudden?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Haha, of course not. Where there is true love, nothing should be allowed to stand in its way.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: No doubt people will offer you a colorful variety of opinions. But of course, you will have factored this into your decision, and I'm sure you are prepared for whatever challenges may lie ahead.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Indeed I am.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: So, please be confident. When your mind is made up, you ought not be worried about things for which you are already well-prepared.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Nevertheless, there is just one small aspect of this that puzzles me a little...

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Please go ahead.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: You've been working hard to bring the Tenryou Commission in line. This is positive, and no doubt the beginning of an important change. But on the other side of this equation, Lady Hiiragi's father, Hiiragi Shinsuke, is still in prison.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: If you choose now, of all moments, to announce a marriage between the Hiiragi and Kujou Clans, the kinds of rumors that may begin to spread, both among the general public and in the Kanjou Commission, are not likely to be in either of your best interests.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Yeah...

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Couldn't have put it better myself, Sir Kamisato. This has been my biggest concern for quite a while now.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Hiiragi Shinsuke is firmly against me having any contact at all with Chisato. In the past, we've always had to communicate in secret, by sending letters.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: So although now may not look like the best timing for this marriage, it may well be the only opportunity we have.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Oh! That guy! Yeah, he acts like this sweet old man, but he was determined to make as much trouble for us as possible! Oh, he is the worst...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I can see where you're coming from. But you're only postponing the problem, not solving it. You will still have to face it sooner or later.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: *sigh* Yes, I'm well aware of that. But since Chisato had the courage to ask me to marry her in spite of everything, how can I disappoint her?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh... so she proposed to you?

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Well, sort of... She raised the idea in a letter, and after some initial hesitation, I went to meet her and have a serious conversation about our future.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: It's funny, actually, because when I formally proposed to her in person, she denied having ever written that letter... Ah, so coy...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? ...Really?

choices.text: I guess she's just pretty shy?

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: She didn't say, she just acted confused by the whole thing. She really committed to it. I'll never forget the look on her face.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Anyway, as her boyfriend, I knew she was just pretending. So, I played along and said "Ah, I was only joking about the letter"... Then, I proposed.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: After making some disgruntled noises about me making a stupid joke, she blushed and said yes. We spent that afternoon working through all the details of the wedding.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Okay. So you discussed it and decided on a date.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: We did. I guess... it was a chance to finally express our commitment to one another, clearly and completely.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: And you know what? I think it was about time.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: No matter what happens next... I will always be there for her as the one person she can always rely on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Argh, gimme a break...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sorry, but Paimon's been wanting to say this the whole time! Is it just this dude, or does everyone in love act like this? He just won't stop talking!

choices.text: Nothing can stop him from sharing his love story...

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Apologies, my friends, and also to Sir Kamisato... I must sound like a fool.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Far from it. On the contrary, seeing you so positively smitten puts my mind at rest.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: No surer evidence could there be of your true feelings and your commitment. If I had any reservations before, I certainly don't now.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I wish you a joyous wedding when the day comes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, even if it's kinda irritating to see you all smug like this, it's still a happy occasion. Good luck on the day, and have a happy wedding!

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Thank you all, it means a lot.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: We have some other business to attend to now. Until next time.

response.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
response.text: Very well. I'll see you out.

choices.text: I think he can't help it.
Maybe she prefers things to be more implicit?
You must be a smooth operator.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He seems busy. That must be true for anyone about to get married, right? It's a happy kind of busy, though.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: You're right. Kujou Kamaji is on cloud nine.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: What do you think, Traveler?

choices.text: He seems genuinely happy, but...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: He chalked it up to her being coy, but... that doesn't sound like the Hiiragi Chisato I know.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: It bothers me also. But unfortunately, attempting to seek the truth of the matter would likely be fruitless.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How so?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, how come? Whenever we come across stuff like this on our adventures, we always find a way to get to the bottom of it.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I see. So that's how adventurers think.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: In my opinion, we face two obstacles in this case. Firstly, we have very little information to go on, and I must be cautious about taking a stance. This makes it difficult to investigate.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Secondly, and more importantly, the person involved doesn't seem to care.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: If we intervene without his blessing, good intentions may lead to catastrophic results.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You do have a point... Kamaji doesn't seem worried at all.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Everything in the world is intertwined. What looks like a simple outcome is often the result of multiple conflating reasons.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Seeking the full truth would be a long and laborious process. It would be inefficient.

choices.text: Speaking from experience?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Sort of. I have to take this approach, or the work of the Yashiro Commissioner would never be done.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: My opinion is something like this: When something strange happens, instead of trying to find out what could have caused it, it is better to look at the situation itself.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: If the outcome is positive, and no one was deceived or harmed in the process, then it is acceptable.

choices.text: But...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: We don't know yet. After all, we don't know what Hiiragi Chisato's thoughts are, do we?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I have to say, I'm impressed by your ability to zero in on the issue from such a short meeting. Most insightful of you. You are thorough and thoughtful, just as my sister describes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But... Chisato and Kamaji have already talked everything through, haven't they?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Only if we are to take Kujou Kamaji at his word. But there are two sides to every story.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I wish to know Hiiragi Chisato's angle on this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Makes sense, but Paimon still doesn't quite get it...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Don't worry about it. I was planning to visit the Hiiragi Clan to deliver my best wishes anyway. Let's take the opportunity to hear her thoughts.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: If she's as committed as Kujou Kamaji, perhaps they can navigate the challenges ahead successfully. But if not...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: ...Well, life isn't always a smooth journey.

choices.text: Are there really no negative consequences to this?
Been here before?
...I'm bothered by how the whole thing began.

talks.objective: Go to the Hiiragi Estate in Ritou

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I know it's not an easy path ahead, but this is my responsibility.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I need to give her a reason to be confident in me.

talks.objective: Talk to members of the Kanjou Commission

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: There is still much to prepare for the wedding.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Should we also invite some prominent business leaders who frequently visit Ritou?

dialogues.speaker: Hishida
dialogues.text: At the very least we should send them invitations.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: I agree... Ah, hello there, Yashiro Commissioner.

dialogues.speaker: Yagi
dialogues.text: To what do we owe the honor on this fine day?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: As it happens, I'm here regarding the same wedding I believe I heard you discussing just now. I come bearing the felicitations of the Kamisato Clan.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Would Lady Hiiragi happen to be available at this moment?

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Our lady is entertaining guests right now, and we're not entirely sure how long she will be.

dialogues.speaker: Hishida
dialogues.text: But please, do come in. We will arrange some tea and snacks for you and your attendants.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Paimon is not an attendant!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: You misunderstand. These two are dear friends.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehehe, you're too kind...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: We don't wish to impose. We'll just wander around in the general area.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Apologies for the interruption while you're busy with preparations. Please let us know once Lady Hiiragi is available.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Nonsense, Commissioner, no imposition at all. This wedding is a joyful occasion, and all the other clans who serve the Hiiragi Clan are most delighted for them indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: We're merely doing the best we can to make this wedding as grand an affair as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Hishida
dialogues.text: When the time comes, we'll invite everyone in the clan and even the general public to attend.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: That sounds splendid.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: We'll leave you to it.

dialogues.speaker: Yagi
dialogues.text: Take care, Commissioner.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your review seemed pretty positive. But Paimon still thinks there are better combinations...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Taste is your key concern, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Obviously! Tasty food and drinks are some of life's most important pursuits.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Well said. If I could say the same was true for me, I believe I'd be a very content man.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In other words, you have too many other things to worry about?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Yes. No one has unlimited energy, and I try to conserve mine for the things that really count. To create some mental breathing room, I try not to overthink the less-critical matters.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Having my sister attend public events in my stead and having Thoma as housekeeper has also been a great help, and allowed me to focus.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're just passing the time here though, right? Is there anything else to think about than what we're doing right now?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: One or two things.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Let's continue this discussion somewhere else.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I noticed something before we left the Hiiragi Clan's residence.

choices.text: You saw who Hiiragi Chisato was meeting?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: No, it was just a small detail. I was curious to know their thoughts on the wedding, so I asked them about it.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Naturally, they responded that all other clans are happy for the Hiiragi Clan...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: But that's not the truth.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you mean?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Hiiragi Shinsuke is still in prison, meaning the Kanjou Commission is the least stable in the Tri-Commission.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Hiiragi Chisato is the sole remaining pillar of her clan, but now she plans to marry into the Kujou Clan. If I belonged to one of the assisting clans to the Hiiragis, I would not be feeling optimistic about the future.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: But they didn't mention a word about that, they simply said they were delighted for them. These are not unintelligent people... I highly doubt it is because they simply do not realize.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hmm, I guess it is a bit strange...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I imagine they didn't want to discuss family issues in front of outsiders. But still, the more I think back over that conversation, the more it doesn't sit right.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Keep a close eye on them, Hisashi.

response.speaker: Hisashi
response.text: Yes, Sir.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! Where did you come from!?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: This is one of my most trusted members of the Shuumatsuban. He's been quietly watching out for us this whole time.

response.speaker: Hisashi
response.text: Merely doing my duty, Sir.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Keep a close watch on the clan representatives we met today.

response.speaker: Hisashi
response.text: Well received. I'm on the case.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Oh, and I almost forgot. That milk I just had — please order one more and deliver it to Thoma.

response.speaker: Hisashi
response.text: As you wish, Sir.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no, poor Thoma!

choices.text: (Sorry, Thoma.)

response.speaker: Yokoyama
response.text: Sir Kamisato, Lady Hiiragi's previous engagement is now concluded. She's waiting for you in the courtyard.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Thank you kindly.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Let's go and see Hiiragi Chisato.

choices.text: (Good luck, Thoma)
You overheard those guys talking about something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi! Nice to see you again, Chisato!

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: I heard that Sir Kamisato had brought some guests, but I didn't know it was you two.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: It's been a while, Lady Hiiragi. How have you been faring?

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: This is a rare privilege, Sir Kamisato. It is not often that I have the chance to meet you, let alone here in the comfort of my own home. I'm doing very well indeed, thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: You must be so busy. Thank you so much for taking the time to come and congratulate Kamaji and I, it really means a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: But of course. The Tri-Commission are the servants of the Shogun, and we should look out for one another. In fact, we visited Sir Kujou just now. It's clear that he's very much looking forward to the wedding.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Perhaps his joy is infectious, for I am now feeling rather elated myself. I sincerely wish you a joyful wedding and a blissful marriage.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Thank you for your kind words.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: This was not an easy decision to make. We will both have to work harder from now on.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: I'm sure the news will cause something of a stir. But come what may, we will stand as one and face whatever the future throws at us together.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like things are pretty tough for you, Chisato.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Yes... To be honest, I'm still a little nervous about it all...

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: But Kamaji has been so supportive. His promises have comforted me a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: It sounds like you have some considerable reservations, Lady Hiiragi.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: ...Yes, well... There are so many things I need to consider.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: In case you were wondering, I was not actually entertaining VIPs just now. I was in fact meeting with one of the Kanjou Commission's officers, Shinnojou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... really? Him?

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. He charged in all of a sudden and said that he had something very important to tell me.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: He didn't mince his words. Basically... he doesn't want me to marry Kamaji.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...He finally went there.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: He has always been a calm and contained person who never acts out of line. I was quite shocked to see him so agitated.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: But despite all that, what he was saying made a lot of sense. He thinks that now is a bad time for this wedding to happen.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: He pointed out that I am like the final pillar propping up my clan. If I marry into the Kujou Clan, that pillar is taken away. There will no longer be a voice of authority in the Hiiragi Clan, and it could be a disastrous move for my personal image, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's just two families becoming one big family though, right? What's the big deal?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Traditionally, in Inazuma, clan affiliation influences every facet of life.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: After the wedding, Lady Hiiragi will belong to the Kujou Clan. The Kanjou Commission's attitude toward you may undergo some significant changes thereafter.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Precisely. This is a terrible thing to be saying, but... I'm starting to have second thoughts. Maybe I went along with it all too easily. Maybe I allowed myself to be pushed into this...

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Ah! I'm so sorry, I can't believe I'm making my guests listen to me complaining...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: No problem at all. The Yashiro Commission has a duty to listen to you. Now that I've heard your concerns, I should offer to help you as best I can, for instance, by helping you gather your thoughts on the matter.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Now. We heard from Sir Kujou that his decision to tie the knot was prompted by a letter he received from you.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: But we've also heard that you did not write that letter. Sir Kujou thought that perhaps you were just being coy... Oh dear, perhaps I should have kept that part to myself?

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: ...What? But that was... It was just a prop in his playful proposal, wasn't it? It was clearly purpose-designed, what with all the fancy lettering, and so on...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: ...Fancy lettering, you say?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: So I am to understand that had it not been for this letter, you two may not have chosen this moment to be wed?

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: When it comes down to it... Yes, I think so... Oh, do you mean to say that this letter is not what I thought it to be?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Sir Kujou maintains that the letter was penned by your hand.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Huh? But then... how did...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Either way, it's wonderful to see how much you both trust one another. In that sense, you could say that the origin of the letter is ultimately not of great importance.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Who knows, perhaps Sir Kujou was the one being coy. After all, he had no particular reason to be forthcoming with us about the details of his playful proposal.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: I understand. As you say, ultimately, the origin of the letter doesn't matter.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: But my position does matter. Kamaji and I thought that we needn't worry about anything that lies ahead, because we can face it all together.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: But now, I... I think I should give it some more thought.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Marriage is the most important decision of your life. Don't let yourself regret it.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: It is also part of the Yashiro Commission's job to help people through difficult times.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I say this as an advocate for you personally and for the Hiiragi Clan. Please do not be compelled by circumstances to make any decision that goes against your will.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: To be together with the one you love is a sacred thing. It is my earnest wish that both of you may enjoy a bright and beautiful future, not a bittersweet one.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: I'll take to heart every word you have said to me... I can't thank you enough, Sir Kamisato. I'll think very carefully about your advice.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: All that matters is that you follow your heart. Since you'll be needing some time to think things over, we will excuse ourselves now.

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Ah, wait! Let me see you out...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Thank you, Lady Hiiragi, but there will be no need.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Traveler, let's find somewhere to talk.

talks.objective: Leave the Hiiragi Estate and go over what you know

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hiiragi Chisato is on a totally different page than Kujou Kamaji...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ayato, why did you give her such vague suggestions? Couldn't you just have told her what you'd do in her position? 'Cause Paimon's pretty sure you have an idea.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I've said everything I can, given the Yashiro Commission's stance. Interfering too much with other Commissions' domestic issues will only create trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: The more I think about it, the stranger this all seems, but Hiiragi Chisato has yet to see it. We must be vigilant.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Strange? In what way?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Someone wants Hiiragi Chisato to be married as soon as possible, and if my guess is right... it is someone from within the Kanjou Commission. This person is presumably also responsible for the mysterious and misleading letter.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Think about this: A lowly officer is greatly worried about Hiiragi Chisato's future, while the heads of the supporting clans ostensibly have no concerns at all. It doesn't add up.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: When someone's words and actions do not match, you need to infer their intentions from their behavior.

choices.text: So... is someone trying to get Hiiragi Chisato into trouble?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Yes. It's a smart strategy. Far superior to the one adopted by the Tenryou Commission's Takatsukasa Clan.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Even had the forged letter failed and been seen for what it was, there would have been no repercussions. They could simply have explained it away as a misguided but well-meaning matchmaking attempt by a member of the family.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: But if the letter were to achieve its goal, as it has so far... the perpetrator would successfully weaken the Hiiragi Clan without ever having to lift a finger against them, all under the guise of simply encouraging a wedding.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: With Hiiragi Chisato having married into the Kujou Clan and the head of the Hiiragi Clan in prison, challenges to the Hiiragi Clan's leadership would begin to emerge throughout the ranks of the Kanjou Commission... Eventually, another clan would take the Hiiragi Clan's place.

choices.text: A reasonable theory. But it's just a theory.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Actually, we have evidence. His name is Shinnojou.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Shinnojou?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: He should be back by now.

response.speaker: Hisashi
response.text: Yes, Sir.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aah! That's the second time you've done that! Paimon cannot deal with this...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Did they take one of the Kanjou Commission officers away?

response.speaker: Hisashi
response.text: Yes. His name is Shinnojou.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: As I expected.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: They cannot afford to let this opportunity pass them by. They have to act now, while the Hiiragi Clan is at its weakest.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Hiiragi Chisato had been persuaded by Kujou Kamaji, and the wedding was sure to go ahead.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: But after Chisato's meeting with Shinnojou, she began to have second thoughts. In their eyes, Officer Shinnojou has interfered with their plan.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why did they suspect him, and not us?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Someone was eavesdropping on our conversation with Chisato the entire time. That's why I was a little reserved.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *gasp* No way! Whew... lucky Paimon didn't say anything stupid.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! But Chisato got what you meant about the letter though, right?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I think so. But whoever is behind this will not allow their plan to fail now. They will not be inclined to respect Hiiragi Chisato's own wishes.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Her stance was so passive that she was easily manipulated... Treated like a pawn, with even her marriage becoming a battleground for political power play.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Despite all of this, she still believed that a happy future was awaiting her...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: When she formally marries into the Kujou Clan, she will lose her title as daughter of the Hiiragi Clan, her position in the Kanjou Commission... and above all, her independence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whew, marriage is such a trap...

choices.text: We've got to stop her.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Easier said than done... The perpetrators are manipulating everything from the shadows, letting unsuspecting pawns do their work. This is what makes their approach so smart.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: We, meanwhile, are out in the open. If we attempt to stop this wedding from happening, we will become the villains of the story and face immense public backlash.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... so what're we gonna do?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: At this stage, if the perpetrators wish to maintain control over the situation, their only option is to come out from the shadows and bare their fangs. I will wait for that moment to arrive.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: But first things first, we must go and rescue Shinnojou. He has done nothing wrong, and does not deserve to be punished.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Tell me where Shinnojou is. We'll head off right now.

choices.text: We can't let this evil plan come to fruition.
Unfortunately, there's no evidence.
So... is someone coveting Hiiragi Chisato's position?

dialogues.speaker: Ippei
dialogues.text: Not to pry, but it seems like there's something on your mind. Do you want to talk about it?

dialogues.speaker: Shinnojou
dialogues.text: It's nothing. I just didn't sleep well, that's all. Really, I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: What's wrong? Are you worried about having to be on your best behavior around my lord? Hahaha, don't be nervous. He's actually pretty easy to get along with.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Well... the vast majority of the time, at least...

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Now, where were we again? Ah yes, invitations...

dialogues.speaker: Hishida
dialogues.text: My family can take charge of that. We have a lot of written correspondence with them already.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Sounds sensible to me. Then, thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you two! Seems like you're always showing up with a VIP in tow.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: I got my license and I'm doing a soft opening today. Wanna try out my latest creative drink?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm a little busy right now...

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Okay sure. Well, feel free to swing by later if you're free.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's Tomoki!

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you! Good to see you again.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Seems like you're always showing up with a VIP in tow.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Oh? So you know the owner as well?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I meant to ask earlier — do you know the owner here as well?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! We tried his Dango Milk a while back with the Almighty Shogun in Inazuma City.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Ah, I see... So you were involved in that...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I'd caught wind of this Dango Milk, but I didn't know that it had anything to do with you two.

choices.text: It was a twist of fate.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I always order one of his creative drinks whenever I pass the stall. The flavor is always new and interesting.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: When I noticed he'd set up shop in Ritou, I simply had to come by.

response.speaker: Tomoki
response.text: Ah, thanks to you all, my business is finally beginning to take off. More and more people are willing to give my creative cuisine a shot.

response.speaker: Tomoki
response.text: It gave me the confidence to decide that I'm gonna stick to creative cuisine from now on.

response.speaker: Tomoki
response.text: On the one hand, I wanted more people to be able to try out my culinary creations. On the other hand, I wanted my customers to experience the joy of being creative, too.

response.speaker: Tomoki
response.text: So, I gave it a lot of thought, and finally came up with an all-new business concept.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Sounds interesting. What is it this time?

response.speaker: Tomoki
response.text: I've decided to give complete creative control to the customer. I offer all sorts of ingredients, and they pick and choose whatever they want to mix with their milk or tea.

response.speaker: Tomoki
response.text: As well as Dango, I now offer Rice Cake, Purple Potato Balls, Black Sugar, and Sunsettia.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do they really all go well with milk...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, hard to imagine. But... who knows — it could be delicious!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: What if I were to choose some ingredients you don't have here? Would that be okay?

response.speaker: Tomoki
response.text: Uhh, well... I guess so. Any novel ideas you have, Commissioner, please feel free to tell me. I'll go buy the ingredients right away.

response.speaker: Tomoki
response.text: The whole idea was to let my customers express their creativity freely. So of course, I shouldn't place restrictions on the ingredients if I can help it.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Excellent. There are a few things I'd like to try...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Lavender Melon, Seagrass, and Sea Ganoderma.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, what? You want to mix those with milk?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I do indeed — why, what's wrong?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...You really think that's gonna turn out tasting good!?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: It's all about the experience — the taste is secondary. It's great to try new things.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Traveler? Any thoughts?

choices.text: It was unexpected, that's for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lavender Melon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like a risky choice. Are you sure...? Well, okay, Paimon will have the same as you...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Three Milks with Lavender Melon, please.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: No problem. Gimme a second, I'll have them ready in just a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a short while, the "Creative Milk" is finally ready.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Here, your milk is ready. Give it a try!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, just as Paimon suspected. Raw Lavender Melon does not taste good!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I think it tastes alright. It makes me feel in touch with mother nature.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seagrass.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you serious? Uh... will Paimon seem like a scaredy-cat if she opts out of this one? Ugh, okay, Paimon'll have one, too...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Three Milks with Seagrass, please.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: No problem. Gimme a second, I'll have them ready in just a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a short while, the "Creative Milk" is finally ready.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Here, your milk is ready. Give it a try!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Seagrass is stuck in the straw... Phew, this is so much work...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: But it tastes alright. It captures the essence of the ocean.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sea Ganoderma.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Doesn't Paimon get a say in this? So this is peer pressure, huh? Well... Alright, then bring it on! Paimon can take it!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Three Milks with Sea Ganoderma, please.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: No problem. Gimme a second, I'll have them ready in just a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a short while, the "Creative Milk" is finally ready.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Here, your milk is ready. Give it a try!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Somehow, Paimon got it down eventually, but... ugh, Paimon feels light-headed...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I think it's alright. It has quite a fascinating texture.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Let's go with Dango.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes! Dango! Dango will do nicely!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Hmm. An ordinary choice, but there's nothing wrong with that.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Two Dango Milks, and one Milk with Lavender Melon, please.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: No problem. Gimme a second, I'll have them ready in just a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a short while, the "Creative Milk" is finally ready.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Here, your milk is ready. Give it a try!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dango Milk tastes pretty good once you get used to it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about yours?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: A most memorable texture indeed. A success, I'd say.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Thanks for coming. Hope to see you again!

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Maybe this whole "creativity" theme really will work out...

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: What should I do...

dialogues.speaker: Hiiragi Chisato
dialogues.text: Oh, Kamaji...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like you guys talked a lot without actually saying anything...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Hence why I dislike small talk.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Our timing was not ideal, but never mind. I spotted a stall on our way over where we can pass the time.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: The owner always manages to come up with novel ideas. I'm one of his regular customers.
